k.q: Debug a storage-device cost-per-GB calculation; the operator is wrong.
k.code:
pricePounds = 60
capacityGB = 1000
costPerGB = pricePounds * capacityGB
print(costPerGB)
p: Correct the expression to calculate cost per GB.
Change pricePounds to 80; calculate the new cost per GB and name one other storage characteristic to consider.
k.a: The incorrect multiplication prints 60,000. Correct statement: costPerGB = pricePounds / capacityGB, which gives £0.06 (6p) per GB for £60 and 1,000 GB. At £80, it gives £0.08 (8p) per GB. Capacity, speed, durability, reliability and portability may also affect choice.

challenge.coreHint: Cost per GB uses price divided by capacity, not multiplied. Compare the printout with a sensible unit.

stretch.task: Compare two illustrative drives: A costs £60 for 1,000 GB and B £80 for 2,000 GB. Debug the calculation and identify the lower price per GB.
stretch.hint: Calculate price / capacity for each, in pounds per GB.
stretch.answer: A = £0.06/GB; B = £0.04/GB. B has the lower cost per GB; it is not automatically the best drive for every purpose.

mastery.task: Debug a program that calculates totals for three purchases but resets total to zero inside its loop. Fix it and add a boundary test for zero quantity.
mastery.hint: Initialise total once before the loop, not each iteration.
mastery.answer: For line costs [4,8,3], correct total15; zero-quantity item adds0; an incorrect reset would leave only the last line cost. Explain where to move the initialisation.
